title: CUDA graph resilience for preemptible streams and fused-attention kernel churn
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem summary:
We intermittently observe incorrect token outputs or crashes when reusing CUDA graphs captured during the prefill stage for multi-stream decoding. Root causes surfaced during triage: 1) non-deterministic kernel selection for fused-attention variants (different kernels selected based on transient allocator state or alignment), 2) capture sequences that are preempted (prefill interrupted by higher-priority work) causing partial graph states, and 3) replay performed on a stream with different runtime kernel routing logic than the capture stream. These manifest as silent corruption during replay or immediate kernel launch failures.

Goal:
Make CUDA-graph capture/replay idempotent and safe across: kernel selector churn, prefill preemption, and cross-stream replay while preserving the steady-state performance benefits of graph replay for multi-stream decode. Provide robust fallback paths and observability so that we can ship without causing regressions in production.

High-level approach (planned):
1) Introduce a capture fingerprint that is persisted with every CUDA graph snapshot. Fingerprint fields: attention-variant-id, kernel-selector-hash, allocator-checksum, prefill-epoch-id, and truncated RNG-seed.
2) During replay, validate the live kernel-selector-hash and attention-variant-id against the fingerprint. If they mismatch, trigger the safe fallback path: replay-on-dynamic (no graph) for this request and enqueue an async "atomic recapture" on a quiescent stream.
3) Add an interruptible-capture protocol: prefill sets a small capture epoch window and publishes a capture-state token to a shared ring. If capture is interrupted, the capture aborts cleanly and increments a capture-failure counter; the runtime will not register the graph as reusable.
4) Provide a deterministic allocator mode used only during capture to stabilize alignment-based kernel selection (lightweight, enabled for capture only). This mode is off in steady-state decode to avoid fragmentation regressions.
5) Add in-graph guard kernels (no-op) that record a compact tracepoint to detect replay order mismatches between capture and replay.

Trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic allocator during capture adds complexity and slightly increases peak transient memory usage but avoids kernel misrouting from alignment differences.
- Atomic recapture increases background work and may lead to slightly higher GPU occupancy transiently; however, it preserves correctness without blocking in-path requests.
- Fingerprinting requires computing and storing small metadata for each graph; negligible storage cost vs. safety benefits.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (Design + spec): finalize fingerprint schema, capture token protocol, and safe-fallback semantics. Design doc linked. (done)
- M2 (Runtime changes): add fingerprint generation, deterministic-capture allocator, guard tracepoints, and fallback policy into the graph manager (WIP).
- M3 (Testing harness): unit + fuzz tests to simulate kernel-selector permutations and preemption scenarios; long-run CI job with 10k randomized captures.
- M4 (Observability + Rollout): add metrics (capture_failures, fallback_triggers, async_recapture_success) + tracing spans; rollout via canary on dedicated capacity.

Observability/metrics required:
- capture.fingerprint.mismatch_count
- capture.interrupted_count
- capture.recapture_attempts / capture.recapture_successes
- decode.replay_fallback_rate (per model and per region)
- trace IDs for capture->recapture correlation

Test plan (details below):
- Deterministic fuzzing harness that enumerates kernel-selector permutations: vary alignment, batch size, seq lengths, GPU architecture flags, and run 1000 randomized capture/replay cycles. Expect 0 mismatches after fixes.
- Canary job: 24h dedicated-capacity canary running mixed traffic with tracing enabled; fallback rate must be <= 0.05% to advance.
- Performance regression tests: end-to-end p50/p95 decode latency with and without deterministic-capture enabled; target <= 1% p50 regression and <= 3% p95 regression for steady-state after warmup.

Rollout strategy:
1) Merge behind runtime feature flag default=false.
2) Enable flag for internal staging and run 10k-capture CI job.
3) Enable on 1 dedicated-pool canary (low traffic) for 24h. Monitor fallback_rate and customer-facing correctness.
4) Gradually increase traffic and enable auto-recapture for graphs that fail validation.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI fuzzing: 10k randomized capture/replay cycles show no silent corruption and fallback triggers < 0.1% with successful async recapture > 95%.
- Canary: decode.replay_fallback_rate <= 0.05% and capture.recapture_success >= 95% over 24h canary run.
- Performance: steady-state p50 latency regression <= 1% vs baseline runtime without changes.

Notes and open questions:
- Should the fingerprint include the kernel binary checksum (slow) or just the selector hash? We decided on selector-hash for speed and smaller metadata; follow-up if selector becomes too coarse.
- How to persist graphs across driver updates? For now graphs are invalidated on driver-major changes; track as follow-up (ENG-????).
- Edge-case: multi-tenant GPUs where another tenant triggers allocator alignment changes mid-capture. Mitigation: deterministic-capture should mask allocator variance; if not, fallback will catch it.
